stem.text: Recombinant DNA technology is used to make recombinant human proteins.
Two of the available methods to obtain the gene of interest are:

items: cutting the gene out of genomic DNA using restriction enzymes
obtaining messenger RNA (mRNA) from cells that are expressing the gene and then using

stem.text: reverse transcriptase to make complementary DNA (cDNA).
Plasmids can be used as vectors to transfer the gene of interest into a host organism.
Recombinant human insulin is a protein that is made using recombinant DNA technology.
Bacteria can be used as host cells to express the recombinant protein.
For the human insulin gene to be successfully expressed in bacteria, one method chosen to obtain the gene is to extract mRNA from β-cells in the pancreas.
The gene coding for insulin is not expressed in the bacterial host when it has been obtained by cutting it out of genomic DNA.
Suggest and explain how the structural difference of cDNA and genomic DNA leads to only cDNA being expressed successfully.

points.text: 1 cDNA has, no introns / only exons or genomic DNA has introns (and exons) ;
2 introns are non-coding sequences / exons are coding sequences ;
3 bacteria cannot, remove introns / carry out splicing ;
4 with cDNA, functional mRNA is made / translation occurs or with genomic DNA, functional mRNA is not made / translation does not occur ;

explanation.text: A coding sequence can be obtained from donor DNA, mature mRNA via reverse transcription, or chemical synthesis. Mature mRNA has already had introns removed in eukaryotes.

reasoningChain: Choose the appropriate source of the coding sequence.
Explain why that source suits the recipient or desired sequence.

inferredMistakes.text: Transferring intron-containing eukaryotic DNA into bacteria without considering RNA processing

stem.text: Plasmids are cut using a restriction enzyme to create sticky ends. The plasmids are mixed with many copies of the desired gene and DNA ligase. The gene is inserted into many plasmids.
State the role of DNA ligase in the formation of recombinant plasmids.

points.text: bond together / anneal, with hydrogen bonds ;
formation of phosphodiester bonds / joins sugar phosphate backbone ;

explanation.text: Restriction enzymes cleave DNA at recognition sites. Ligase seals the sugar–phosphate backbone after compatible DNA ends have paired; the enzymes do different jobs.

reasoningChain: Identify which enzyme cuts and which joins.
Trace the gene into the vector and recipient.

inferredMistakes.text: Saying that DNA ligase cuts the plasmid

stem.text: Explain why a promoter, as well as the gene, may have to be transferred into the plasmid.

explanation.text: A promoter provides a site for transcription machinery to bind. The recipient must recognise it for the transferred coding sequence to be transcribed.

reasoningChain: Connect recognition by the recipient to transcription of the introduced gene.

inferredMistakes.text: Calling a promoter a sequence that directly translates protein

stem.text: Explain how a marker gene coding for a fluorescent product could be used.

points.text: 1 marker gene is added to plasmid ;
4 when marker gene is expressed fluorescent proteins are made ;
5 ref. to (fluorescent proteins) fluoresce / glow, with exposure to, UV / blue, light ;
6 shows which, bacteria / cells, are transformed / AW ;

explanation.text: A fluorescent marker gives an observable signal of expression under the chosen conditions. Its presence in a construct and its expression are distinct observations.

reasoningChain: Explain how the visible signal is used to identify suitable cells.

inferredMistakes.text: Assuming that fluorescence measures every function of the desired protein

stem.text: The unicellular fungus Saccharomyces cerevisiae is a species of yeast that has been used to produce human insulin. S. cerevisiae cells are able to take up recombinant plasmids.
Suggest advantages of using yeast compared to using bacteria for human insulin production.

points.text: 1 easier / cheaper, to culture yeast cells ;
3 easier, to extract / processing / to purify, (insulin) ;
4 yeast cell similar to β-cells / named example ; e.g. have Golgi apparatus

explanation.text: Successful gene transfer requires a sequence that the recipient can express. Production systems also differ in growth conditions and their ability to process proteins.

reasoningChain: Connect the introduced genetic material to expression.
Relate the recipient’s properties to the intended product.

inferredMistakes.text: Assuming that DNA transfer guarantees a functional protein product
